coverage.instrument: A live AWS node (comp-kuzu's served CloudNode projection, layer aws) is INVOLVED in subject S when at least one of four legs reaches it, MINUS one exclusion. IDENTIFIERS(S) = S's registry spellings long and short from infra/logic/registry/scopes.json (for 49financial: '49financial', '49f'; word-bounded, case-insensitive) plus the run's --seed bucket names. The vendor alias 'bd' is NOT an identifier: it is the blackdiamond vendor's abbreviation shared with cottonwood and inflection (e.g. bd-cot-keepalive-sched), so it is a pointer to a vendor, not to S. (1) token: comp-find --corpus aws finds an identifier in the node's name, ARN or properties; a comp-trigger --list EventPattern naming one counts the same. (2) iam_grant: a LIVE role an APPLIED Allow statement of which names an identifier in its Resources, or that holds (comp-kuzu HAS_POLICY) a token-leg IAM_POLICY; every compute node that ASSUMES such a role (comp-kuzu ASSUMES; an EC2 through its instance profile, HAS_PROFILE) is involved, and every involved compute node's own execution role is involved as its identity (that reverse step does NOT fan out to the role's other users). (3) source_text: a Lambda whose packaged source files (infra/aws/lambda/ci/lambda-source-map.json source_dir + files) carry an identifier in a whitespace-free CODE string literal -- an address, a prefix, a bucket, a firm key; a comment, a docstring or a prose guard message that names S to stay out of it is not a reach. (4) trigger_target: an EVENT_RULE or SCHEDULE whose target is an involved COMPUTE node (a shared sink such as an alert topic does not pull in every rule that publishes to it), and every target of an involved trigger or of an involved bucket's notification (comp-kuzu TRIGGERS/EMITS_TO, plus comp-trigger's LIVE list-targets-by-rule), iterated to a fixpoint. EXCLUDED: a LOG_GROUP under /aws/lambda/ or /aws/ -- the runtime's own per-function sink, which carries the token only because AWS names it after its function; it holds no subject data, is read or written by nothing in the subject's data path, and is re-created by migrating its function, which IS a row. An involved node whose node_type is outside the contract's node_type enum is NOT_COVERED, never dropped. THE AUTHORIZATION PLANE (LT-e-6, round 4; ruling R-81 assigns authorization to comp-iam live / comp-iam reconcile / comp-iam simulate ONLY). The iam_grant leg reads the LIVE plane, never the repo's declared one: a vintage-stamped live IAM census (one read-only iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, stamped at the read by the reader's own clock) is admitted only after comp-iam reconcile's fail-closed vintage gate PASSES on it -- a refusal (rc 3) refuses this leg rather than degrading it -- and comp-iam live supplies the served graph's live role population beside it as the cross-check neither read can perform on itself. DISCLOSED BLIND SPOT, never silently inherited: that census expands INLINE policy documents and RECORDS an attached-managed policy as UNRESOLVED with no Resources text, so a subject grant reachable ONLY through an attached managed policy is not reached by this leg's resource match; the HAS_POLICY sub-leg still reaches it whenever the policy itself carries a token. THE HAND SURFACE (R-81: a hand-maintained input is GUARDED or DECLARED, no third option). lambda-source-map.json, the source_text leg's only input, is GUARDED: comp-lambdamap check runs on every walk over two independent planes (the map against the Terraform tree and the on-disk source directories), its named drift classes and their counts are carried in this contract's coverage.hand_surfaces, and a guard that does not run is reported as UNMEASURED rather than as clean. The guard is what makes the leg's reach falsifiable: a function the map omits is invisible to source_text, and a TOTAL comparison cannot see it -- the map's count and the live count nearly agree while their NAMES disagree.
